1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4.strategy: The natural recapture: the knight takes the centre and the bishops and queen get open lines. It will be harassed by Black's developing moves, so White's piece set-up must be ready to meet them, but the central knight also supports a later attack.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.c3.strategy: A gambit that offers a pawn for a lead in development and an open c-file. Black keeps a real extra pawn that White must justify by quick development, so the idea only works if White's pieces come out faster than Black can untangle.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.c3.name: Sicilian Defence: Smith-Morra Gambit Deferred

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 a6.strategy: A flexible waiting move: it rules out Nb5 and prepares ...b5, and Black delays developing the knights until White commits. The cost is a tempo that does not develop a piece; Black bets on a compact structure and counterplay on the queenside.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nc6.strategy: Develops with pressure on the d4-knight and keeps all of Black's options open for the bishops and the queen. White can challenge or exchange the knight, but Black gets natural development in a flexible position.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nf6.strategy: Develops with an attack on e4 and stops the quick e5 push, since ...Qa5+ would then win the pawn. Black keeps a flexible set-up and makes White defend the e-pawn before anything else.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qb6.strategy: A sharp surprise weapon: the queen hits the d4-knight and the b2-pawn at once and prepares to bring the bishop to bear on f2. A calm retreat of the knight to b3 takes the sting out, and Black has committed the queen early.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qb6.name: Sicilian Defence: Kveinis Variation
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Qb6.background: A pet line of the Lithuanian International Master Aloyzas Kveinys (1962–2018), it has also been played by strong grandmasters including Nigel Short and Judit Polgar.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Bc5.strategy: Develops with an attack on the d4-knight, but the knight can retreat with a gain of time. It is an offbeat way to develop that leaves Black chasing the initiative, though the position stays playable.
1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 e6 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 Bc5.name: Sicilian Defence: Paulsen-Basman Defence
